text:
alyssa: Heads-up — saw repeating memory spikes on dedicated with llama-13b-mqa when feeds hit ~32k tokens. KV residency seems to oscillate rather than converge. Repro on canary with rope-scale=1.00025 (old runs stable).

rob: How big are the spikes? plateaus or progressive growth?

alyssa: Spikes ~2.4GB per 5k tokens, then a drop, then back up. After ~120k tokens net memory is +6GB vs baseline. Observed on both GQA and MQA, but larger with MQA.

cheng: @alyssa can you paste the profiler slice? also which kernel selection path?

alyssa: Here are the quick notes from the canary run:
```
perf: kv_resident_pages: 24->46->28->50->30->52...
kernel: opt_conv_v2 for attn; fallback to matmul_small when seq>4096
batching: continuous-batch enabled
cmd: ./run_canary --model llama-13b-mqa --rope-scale 1.00025 --seq 131072
```

sara: Maybe eviction sweep isn't triggering because of page reference jitter. Could be rope scaling causing false new prefixes.

perf-bot: [anomaly] eviction_rate variance > 3x over last hour. trace_id=abc123. Suggested: capture kv-page-trace.

rob: Try forcing KV compaction after X tokens: set KVCOMPACT_INTERVAL=8192 and rerun?

alyssa: Ran with KVCOMPACT_INTERVAL=4096 — drops the oscillation but latency tail increases ~6% and some generation stalls.

cheng: We should collect a memmap of page ownership. Can you run with --kv-trace=pages and attach? @ops-bot can we spin a 4x canary?

ops-bot: Canary spun: run id canary-365432; 4x gpus reserved. Link: https://ci.internal/canary-365432

sara: Also check kernel selection logs. If kernel switch happens mid-seq we might be duplicating KV layouts due to differing slot packing.

alyssa: Attached limited trace (trimmed):
```
[0] alloc_page(owner=attn_kv, slot=12)
[1] alloc_page(owner=attn_kv, slot=13)
...
[246] kernel_switch matmul_small -> opt_conv_v2
[247] alloc_page(owner=attn_kv, slot=27)
[248] sweep: reclaimed 0 pages (ref_count noise)
[249] alloc_page(owner=attn_kv, slot=28) -> increased resident
```

rob: Hypothesis: MQA's quant-blocking causes non-deterministic page fragmentation pattern; when rope scale slightly >1, token hashes shift and cause new page owners instead of reuse.

cheng: Action items: (1) reproduce with KVCOMPACT_INTERVAL disabled, (2) capture kernel selection timeline, (3) add a no-op compaction that is latency-budgeted. I'll take (3).

alyssa: I'll repro and upload full traces to the canary link. thanks :thumbsup:

sara: FYI if we confirm kernel-induced fragmentation we can try aligning slot packing between kernels as a mitigation (low-risk).

rob: Also add a micro-benchmark that runs deterministic rope perturbations so we can unit-test this regression.

alyssa: Sounds good — starting the longer run now, will ping when complete.
